chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from 'Abis ibn Hisham, from more than one person, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

The readers of the Quran are of three types: A man who read the Quran and took it as merchandise, used it to attract the rulers and to lord over the people. A man who read the Quran, memorized its letters but wasted its limits. And a man who read the Quran and applied the medicine of the Quran to the illness of his heart, kept vigil through the night by it, endured thirst during the day, stood in prayer in his mosques, and forsook his bed for its sake. Through such people Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repels calamities; through them Allah grants victory over the enemies; and through them Allah sends down rain from the sky. By God, such people in their recitation of the Quran are more precious than red sulfur.

key_terms.الكبريت الأحمر: Red sulfur — a proverbially rare alchemical substance, used as a metaphor for extreme rarity and preciousness
key_terms.بضاعة: Merchandise, commodity — here used metaphorically for exploiting the Quran for worldly gain
key_terms.حدود: Limits, boundaries — the rules, commandments and principles contained in the Quran
key_terms.دواء: Medicine, remedy — the Quran described as a cure for spiritual ailments

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Quran readers according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) classifies Quran readers into three categories in this hadith narrated at a scholarly gathering in Muharram 368 AH: those who exploit it for worldly gain and influence over rulers, those who memorize its text but ignore its commandments, and those who internalize it as spiritual medicine. The third group, who pray through the night, fast during the day, and forsake comfort for the Quran's sake, are described as the instruments through whom God repels calamities, defeats enemies, and sends rain — making them rarer and more precious than red sulfur, the rarest alchemical substance in classical Islamic culture.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. `Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah from Isma`il b. Mehran from `Isa b. Hisham from another person from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as). He said:

The readers of the Quran are of three types: (1) One is a man who has learned the Quran and has taken it as a piece of merchandise to attract the rulers and dominate the people. (2) One is a man who has learned the Quran and preserved its letters but has lost its principles. He has kept its letters without change, [but I pray that] Allah does not increase the number of people like him as the carriers of the Quran. (3) One is a man who has applied the medicine of the Quran to the malady of his heart. It keeps him vigilant during the night, it makes him endure his thirst during the day, it keeps him standing [in prayer] in the mosques, and it makes him leave his bed for its sake. Through such people, Allah repels calamities; through them, Allah defends [the people] from the enemies; and through them, He sends down rain from the sky. By Allah, such readers of the Quran are more valuable than red sulfur.
